Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)

  • Transient rash on posterior calf mid–late Feb (photo shown); faded over ~2 weeks; minimal itch; preceded by mild sore throat ± low-grade fever; possible tick exposure while hiking in USA (late Jan)  
  • Occasional headaches; able to work but reports reduced concentration/energy  
  • Past medical history: asthma (well-controlled), allergic rhinitis/hay fever  
- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  
  • Preventive asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (patient uses morning and night)

  • OTC antihistamine – name/dose/frequency not documented  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Lives with wife; no other sexual history documented.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Previously very active (walking/hiking); recent reduction in exercise; eating smaller portions.

  • Alcohol – occasional use  
  • Tobacco – not recorded (patient did not give clear answer)  
  • Other substances – not recorded

- Vision problems or recent changes: Denies blurred vision or visual changes.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Lives with wife; employed at a health technology company; no caring responsibilities reported.

Management Plan

- Arrange venous blood collection for CBC, renal panel, liver panel, and Lyme disease serology.

- If Lyme serology positive: commence appropriate antibiotic regimen (to be determined upon results).

- No immediate medications started; current asthma management to continue.

● Transcript quality: Some speech drop-outs and unfinished sentences, but core clinical information was understandable.
